findings.claim: In January 2000 Koch Industries agreed to a $30 million civil penalty, which EPA called the largest then imposed on a company under any federal environmental law, over more than 300 oil spills from its pipelines and facilities in six states. The settlement is more than 25 years old.

In April 2001 Koch Petroleum Group, with Koch Industries, pleaded guilty to concealing Clean Air Act benzene violations at its Corpus Christi refinery in 1995, and agreed to $10 million in criminal fines, $10 million for local environmental projects and five years of probation.

In March 2014 Flint Hills Resources, a Koch Industries company, settled US claims of excess benzene and other hazardous emissions from flares at its Port Arthur, Texas chemical plant, with a $350,000 civil penalty and controls EPA expected to cut about 1,900 tons of pollutants a year.

OpenSecrets reported in August 2024 that Koch Industries gave $25 million in 2024 to Americans for Prosperity Action, the Koch network’s hybrid super PAC, which by early August had spent about $62 million supporting Republican candidates that cycle and none supporting Democrats.

Charles Koch told Forbes in October 2023 that over four years he had moved about $5.3 billion of nonvoting Koch Industries stock to two nonprofits, including $4.3 billion to the 501(c)(4) Believe in People. Such groups may lobby and spend on politics if politics is not their primary focus; the figures are his own.

Popular Information reported that gifts to 501(c)(4) groups have been exempt from federal gift tax since a 2015 law, and that Believe in People had no public filings. Its view that the structure let Koch avoid tax is a press analysis, not an official finding.

Documents released in 2018 showed older Charles Koch Foundation gift agreements let it appoint members of a committee recommending Mercatus Center professors at George Mason University, and of a board that could recommend dismissals. The university president said they fell short of its standards; both say newer agreements lack these terms.
IRS filings show the Charles Koch Foundation, chaired by Charles Koch, reported about $423 million in charitable disbursements from 2020 to 2024, including $67.8 million in 2024.

ecology.reason: Koch Industries runs oil refineries, pipelines and chemical plants through units such as Flint Hills Resources. It paid a then-record $30 million civil penalty in 2000 over more than 300 oil spills, a unit pleaded guilty in 2001 to concealing benzene violations at a Texas refinery, and a 2014 EPA settlement covered flare emissions. The group’s current emissions are not quantified here.

politics.reason: Koch Industries gave $25 million in 2024 to Americans for Prosperity Action, the Koch network’s super PAC (OpenSecrets). Charles Koch told Forbes in 2023 that he moved $5.3 billion in stock to two nonprofits, including $4.3 billion to the 501(c)(4) Believe in People, which may engage in politics; how it spends the money is not public. Older Charles Koch Foundation agreements let it appoint members of a committee recommending Mercatus Center professors at George Mason.

legal.reason: A Koch Industries unit pleaded guilty in 2001 to concealing Clean Air Act violations at its Corpus Christi refinery, and Koch Industries paid a then-record $30 million environmental civil penalty in 2000. Both are more than 25 years old; the later EPA settlement found here is small. No personal legal record was found.

unresolved.reason: Believe in People, which Charles Koch says received $4.3 billion in Koch Industries stock, had no public filings as of October 2023, so how the gift is used is not known. Popular Information argues the structure avoided gift and capital gains taxes; that is press analysis, not an official finding.

proposal.counterweights: The Charles Koch Foundation reported about $423 million in charitable disbursements from 2020 to 2024 (IRS filings).
proposal.rationale: Legal 0 to 2: the rubric places a corporate plea at level 2, and a Koch unit pleaded guilty in 2001 (DOJ, EPA); the 2000 penalty was then a record. Both are old, which could argue for a lower value. Ecology 4, politics 3 and open questions 1 are unchanged, now documented. Politics combines the company’s super PAC money with the stock gifts Charles Koch himself disclosed to Forbes, as relayed by his own network and by Sludge.

results.comment: EPA enforcement page (19 Jan 2025 snapshot): settlement filed 13 Jan 2000; Koch Industries, Inc. to pay a $30 million civil penalty, described by EPA as the largest civil fine then imposed on a company under any federal environmental law, over more than 300 spills from pipelines and oil facilities in TX, OK, KS, MO, LA and AL. Company level and settlement type correct.

DOJ release 01-153 (9 Apr 2001): Koch Petroleum Group, L.P. pleaded guilty over concealing 1995 Clean Air Act benzene violations at the Corpus Christi West Plant; $10 million criminal fine, $10 million for local projects, five years probation. EPA release (13 Apr 2001) names Koch Industries, Inc. and Koch Petroleum Group as pleading, which supports "with Koch Industries". Guilty plea, company level.

EPA enforcement page (snapshot): announced 20 Mar 2014; complaint alleges violations at three steam-assisted flares at the FHR Port Arthur chemical plant causing excess VOC and HAP (incl. benzene) emissions; $350,000 civil penalty; about 1,900 tons a year of reductions; page says FHR is ultimately owned by Charles and David Koch of Koch Industries.

Raw Story page carries the OpenSecrets article by Maia Cook (with Anna Massoglia), 12 Aug 2024, with the notice that it originally appeared in OpenSecrets; no Raw Story commentary added. opensecrets.org and the Wayback Machine could not be fetched, but an independent republication (InDepthNH) gives the same figures: Koch Industries $25M to AFP Action in 2024, about $62M supporting Republicans as of 6 Aug 2024, none supporting Democrats. Judged faithful. Label changed to "OpenSecrets via Raw Story" so the republication shows; publisher_type ngo kept for the author, publisher field names Raw Story. The article does not name FEC filings, so "from FEC filings" was removed from the politics reason.

Rewritten: Stand Together (10 Oct 2023) is Koch-founded, so publisher_type changed from ngo to company. It relays the Forbes exclusive: $5.3B of nonvoting stock to two nonprofits over four years, $4.3B to Believe in People, the largest disclosed 501(c)(4) gift. Sludge (10 Oct 2023) cites Koch telling Forbes and gives the 501(c)(4) rule. Neither calls the second recipient (CCKc4, $975M in 2020) a 501(c)(4), so "two 501(c)(4) nonprofits" became "two nonprofits"; the claim now says the figures are his own statement. Level individual and company_disclosure (self-disclosure via his own network) kept.

Popular Information (Legum and Zekeria, 11 Oct 2023): the 501(c)(4) gift-tax exemption was put into a December 2015 omnibus spending law; Believe in People has no publicly available filings; it argues the gifts were structured to avoid capital gains or gift taxes. Claim correctly labels that as press analysis. Proposal reasons no longer say both groups lacked filings.

AP (Matthew Barakat) via Christian Science Monitor, 4 May 2018: released documents show the Koch Foundation could appoint members of a selection committee recommending Mercatus Center professors and of an advisory board that could recommend dismissals; President Cabrera said the agreements fall short of academic-independence standards; GMU and the foundation say newer agreements lack those provisions. Foundation level correct.

ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer (990-PF data): "Charitable Disbursements" of $108.7M (2020), $99.4M (2021), $69.1M (2022), $77.7M (2023), $67.8M (2024), total about $422.7M, so "about $423 million" holds; Charles G Koch listed as chair or director/chairman each year. This is the 990-PF charitable-disbursements figure (money paid out), not total expenses; a grants-paid line alone was not shown.
